en.title: Create from Markdown
en.desc: Paste Markdown from your AI, hover "Create MD" and it becomes a fully typeset document. Three fallback channels adapt to the environment, so a single Ctrl+V still works under local file://.
en.them: Copy → open editor → save → drag into reader
en.us: Copy, hover, click — a document in three steps

en.title: Tables to six charts
en.desc: Select two columns and a chart appears: bar / line / trend / rounded donut / Nightingale rose, with automatic type selection. Donut sectors accumulate angles by percentage, so you can verify them with a protractor.
en.them: A previewer that only gives you a static table
en.us: Angle equals percentage; the data stands up to scrutiny

en.title: Dual-engine flowcharts
en.desc: Mermaid, text arrows and Unicode box-drawing all feed one editable vector diagram; 5 structures × 5 styles = 25 looks.
en.them: Diagramming tools need internet, subscriptions and export dead images
en.us: Pure local recognition — no calls, no waiting, still editable

en.title: One palette, everywhere
en.desc: Four document styles do more than recolor the accent: section backgrounds, chart palettes, flowchart accents and code keywords all change together.
en.them: One document with three blues and two reds
en.us: Changing style never produces dark text on dark ground

en.title: Native wiki links
en.desc: Obsidian [[links]], ![[embeds]], Callouts, YAML frontmatter and #tags render out of the box; drop in a library of thousands of files and it just reads.
en.them: Import the whole vault first, then install a pile of community plugins
en.us: Drop in a folder to build the tree; open it and it reads

en.title: Exports stay alive
en.desc: Standalone HTML keeps its interactions — switch chart types, copy CSV, sort tables; Word and print PDF keep the layout, and SVG plus Markdown source export in one click.
en.us: Export = a clone of the current DOM, i.e. your last edit

en.title: MCP connector
en.desc: mdlens speaks CLI / HTTP / MCP, so AI tools render Markdown straight into pages; the engine is inlined locally.
en.them: Reading pipes and backticks inside a chat window
en.us: The agent renders; you only proofread

en.title: Outline & block editing
en.desc: Click any heading in the sidebar outline to jump; editing is split into independent blocks and only the affected one re-renders, so huge tables stay in order.
en.them: The whole file in one textarea; one save and the diff explodes
en.us: Block-level edits dirty only that block

en.title: Two classic layouts
en.desc: Card = sectioned panel with dark numbered headers; Paper = drafting sheet with binding marks and serif titles. Colors, fonts and radii switch as a set.
en.them: A "skin" that just changes a border color
en.us: Serif / sans, rounded / square — switched as a set

en.title: Recent, re-read from disk
en.desc: Up to 30 entries. Clicking history re-reads the file from disk by absolute path rather than opening a stale snapshot; if the file moved it falls back to the cached body.
en.them: A cached snapshot that still shows the old content
en.us: What you changed yesterday is what you see today

en.title: All 15 preferences remembered
en.desc: Language, layout, font size 12–22px, four line heights, skin, soft light, chart auto-expand, flowchart structure and style — in three grouped cards, each explained in plain words.
en.them: A screen of jargon switches nobody understands
en.us: Everything remembered locally — no login, no upload

en.title: Focus mode
en.desc: Hide the sidebar and toolbar in one click, leaving only the text and reading progress; the render menu still works, because focus should not mean losing features.
en.them: Collapse the panels and the features vanish too
en.us: Cut only the noise, not the capability

en.title: Original Soft Light
en.desc: Soft light covers the toolbar, sidebar, tab bar, reading area and overlays with none left out; the gradient stays continuous, with no visible patch.
en.them: Night mode = darker background, brighter text
en.us: One continuous gradient across the app, stackable with all three themes

en.title: Kind to your eyes
en.desc: Eye care is a low-blue warm beige (card #faf3e0 / paper #fdf3d8 with an amber accent), unmistakably different from plain white.
en.them: Any white background with a hint of yellow called eye care
en.us: Three complete themes, not a filter pasted on top

en.title: International editions
en.desc: Simplified Chinese / English / follow system. Replacements run longest-key first, and missing entries keep the Chinese original instead of showing undefined.
en.them: Half machine-translated UI that translates your text too
en.us: UI text only; document bodies stay untouched
